title: Half-baked API dialect for hardware profiles
content:
Context: This is a scratchpad for a tiny API dialect that we can use between onramp/router and the runtime selection layer. Purpose is to let the router express hardware/quantization preferences plus soft constraints (latency/cost) in a compact way so the runtime can pick a model variant + node pool quickly.

High-level goals: - Extremely compact (<= 3 fields in hot-path) so probes/telemetry stay small. - Express hard requirements (e.g., must be on-prem, specific GPU family) and soft preferences (minimize cost, prefer fp16). - Allow quick fallback semantics when exact match not available. - Support per-request overrides and tenant-level defaults.

Problems this tries to solve: - Router currently has to encode long config blobs or call a heavyweight profile service. Slow. - Dispatch needs to be cheap (millions qps potential). - Need to support both hosted (cloud pools) and private on-prem variants.

Draft API shape (compact): - Purpose: a compact header or small JSON object attached to request metadata. - Keep field names short for wire efficiency.

Example (as small JSON-like token set): hp: A100:80g   // hardware hint (short canonical token) qc: int8q      // quantization/precision hint (one token) s: latency<200|cost~low // soft policy expression (pipe-separated)

Field list (expanded): - hp (hardware-profile): string token mapping to a known profile. Examples: A100:80g, H100:80g, t4:16g, cpu:48c. Router can send a family-level token like A100 to indicate hardware family only. - qc (quant-config): token like fp16, int8q, bnb2, gptq8, q4_0. It's a hint, not a hard requirement unless accompanied by a pref flag. - s (soft-policy): small expression language for quick scoring: operators allowed: <, <=, ~ (approx), | (or), & (and). Examples: latency<100|cost~low. Evaluate top-to-bottom with simple heuristics. - p (priority): optional short int string (p:5) to indicate request priority for admission. - d (durable): optional 0|1 meaning result/call must be on private/dedicated capacity (1) or ok on shared (0).

Compact header example (HTTP): X-Rwd-HP: hp=A100:80g;qc=int8q;s=latency<200|cost~low;d=0;p=10

Resolution rules (runtime side, rough): 1) If d==1 -> limit to dedicated/private pools only (fail fast if none). 2) Try exact hp+qc match in running model variants. If found and node has capacity -> route. 3) If not found, consult fallback table: prefer same family then lower qc then higher latency. 4) Evaluate soft-policy string: compute score for candidate pool: score = baseScore - penalty(latency_violation) - costWeight * costEstimate + preferenceBonus(qc_match) + tenancyBonus. Pick highest score above threshold.

Examples of policies and fallbacks: - Request: hp=A100:80g;qc=int8q;s=latency<50|cost~low;d=0 -> likely no match (very tight latency); runtime may lower qc to fp16 and pick a closer region node pool if cost~low can be traded for lower latency. - Request: hp=t4:16g;qc=fp16;s=cost~low;d=0 -> runtime consolidates to densest packing with t4 pools and picks cheapest cluster.

Schema for expressive mapping table (runtime config, not hot path): - token -> descriptor mapping (kept in memory) - A100:80g -> family:A100;vram_gb:80 - int8q -> method:quant;bits:8;(Keep these in the runtime; router only sends tokens).

ASCII flow diagram: client -> (request + X-Rwd-HP) router (cheap eval) -> quick rejects if d==1 and tenant has no private -> forward to runtime-proxy -> runtime-proxy (hot fast path): - look up token maps - check live pool index (L1 cache) - score candidates using soft-policy - immediate route or respond with fallback advice (if caller supports async requeue)

Notes / heuristics: - Token vocabulary needs governance. Short tokens reduce wire cost but require global registry (versioned). Small registry (~100 tokens) OK. - Soft-policy should be intentionally fuzzy; keep cost/latency weights tunable via runtime flags. - Prefer returning a small set of fallback tokens when routing fails instead of a giant config blob. Example: fallback: [A100,H100,fp16].

API extension: per-tenant defaults and overrides - Tenant has a short profile token assigned at account creation, e.g., TPL:fast-latency or TPL:cost-saver. Router attaches tenant token if no explicit hp. - Router precedence: explicit request headers > tenant defaults > global default.

Open questions / TODOs: - How to version tokens safely so old clients still route to compatible pools? Add a version number in header: v=2. - Would an integer-encoded bitfield for qc/hp be even smaller? Maybe but opaque and harder to extend. - Telemetry: emit resolution path as a 3-token string: sel=A100:int8q:pool42 for cheap ingestion. Keep details in sidecar logs only. - Security: ensure header can't be abused to request on-prem resources. Enforce tenant entitlement checks in runtime-proxy. - Backpressure: if score < threshold, return 429 with small retry-with hints (list of fallback tokens).

Unpolished sketch of HTTP 429 payload: { code:429, retry_with:[A100:fp16,H100:int8q,cpu:48c], msg:"no immediate capacity" }

Bench thoughts: - Hot-path code must optimize token->descriptor lookup (hash map) and candidate scoring (precompute static penalties). - Keep policy expression evaluation lightweight; maybe compile common policy forms into small bytecodes.

Next steps: - Build a small in-process mapper in the router that maps tenant->token + enriches request with X-Rwd-HP. - Prototype runtime-proxy scoring with fake pools (rust or go) and microbench to validate <200ns overhead added. - Draft token registry schema and simple governance process.

Notes to self: this is intentionally minimal; the goal is a pragmatic, wire-efficient contract that gets us out of heavy config bloat in the router. Keep it reversible and versionable. End of scratchpad.
